title: 22.2: An 850µW 2-to-5GHz Jitter-Filtering and Instant-Toggling Injection-Locked Quadrature-Clock Generator for Low-Power Clock Distribution in HBM Interfaces
problem: HBM (high-bandwidth memory) interfaces require parallel distribution of four quadrature clocks across multiple data groups, consuming significant power, introducing quadrature error, and suffering power-supply-induced jitter during long routings.
motivation: Next-generation HBM4 and AI accelerators demand 2TB/s+ bandwidth using thousands of DQ pins, necessitating efficient multi-group clock distribution with minimal jitter and quadrature error.
method: The system uses injection-locking (locking one oscillator to match another's frequency) to build a quadrature-clock generator operating at 2-5GHz. Instead of sending four pre-made clocks across long distances (which causes timing errors), it sends a single reference signal (WDQS) to each data group, where a local generator creates all four clocks on-site. This approach filters out timing jitter (unwanted variations in clock edges) through the locking mechanism and can instantly switch between clock phases when needed.
key_novelty: The injection-locking approach with instant-toggling eliminates the need for separate circuits to fix quadrature errors, instead handling jitter filtering, error correction, and power savings in a single design.
contributions: Achieved 850µW power consumption for clock distribution across all DQ groups
Integrated jitter filtering and instant-toggling capability
Eliminates need for bulky separate QE-corrector circuits per group
Scalable to HBM4 with multiple clock groups
primary_theme: low-power injection-locked clock generation for HBM interfaces
